# Source: PLAN-001-effect-disclosure.md "### W2.3", PLAN-001.dagr.json W2.3's criteria; pattern 011 acceptance-ce9cb247.
# This file is hashed (predictions.tsv.sha256) and the hash is the first line of sequence.log after the type-check note.
# It is not edited after that. A prediction that turns out wrong is a prediction miss in mutants.tsv.
# BEFORE THE HASH, and nothing else: every edit was checked to occur once (scripts/apply-check.txt) and
# type-checked with `ailang check src/core/tool_phase.ail` (runs/typecheck-*.log), and the reach probe
# was type-checked. No gate, no probe and no test was RUN before this file was hashed.
# THE BASIS of every member set below is READING, not a run of this tree: the bank's own selection
# comments (`corpus_pr_dst.fixed_bank()`), the CORPUSROW classes and the `applied_faults` lists of the
# same bank recorded at 034 W1.7 (`../mutation-w1-f160eebb/runs/C-baseline/{bank,cp}.log`), and W2.2's
# measured COUNT (13 pairs: 8 to applied, 5 to not; commit 8c996274's message). Nothing since W1.6
# changed the generator, so the bank is assumed unchanged; if it moved, the member sets below miss.
# Members (18), as `JUDGE` labels: seed-1 seed-3 seed-4 seed-6 seed-8 seed-11 seed-14 seed-18 seed-29
#   seed-31 seed-60 seed-61 seed-71 seed-102 seed-109 seed-165 seed-215 constructed-empty-terminal
# APPLIEDFAILED3 = seed-102 seed-165 seed-215    an after-dispatch ToolFailed the world APPLIED
#                                                (tool_effect_applied_then_failed; applied ordinals 15, 17, 32)
# TOOLFAULT11    = seed-3 seed-11 seed-14 seed-18 seed-60 seed-61 seed-71 seed-102 seed-109 seed-165 seed-215
#                  every member whose classes hold a dispatched tool fault: ToolCorrelationMismatch (3, 18, 215),
#                  a deadline applied (11, 14) or not (60, 109, 215), a ToolFailed applied (102, 165, 215) or not (61, 71)
# DEADLINE5      = seed-11 seed-14 seed-60 seed-109 seed-215    a ToolDeadlineExceeded, applied or not
# FAILED5        = seed-61 seed-71 seed-102 seed-165 seed-215   the twin pairs on an after-dispatch ToolFailed:
#                  61 and 71 flip not -> applied, 102, 165 and 215 flip applied -> not
# OK3OFFAILED5   = seed-71 seed-102 seed-165                     the members of FAILED5 whose run ends Ok
# ALL18          = every member
# Controls of corpus_judge (4, as `CONTROL` labels): retry-with-two-steps-left no-retry-with-one-step-left
#   tool-run-without-approval solver-feedback
# Two gates are run on every row, on the same tree, side by side: `make corpus_judge` (P1 and P3 are rules
# of `dst_invariants.evaluate`, which it runs on every member and control) and `make applied_twin` (P2).
# Scoring rules, fixed here:
#  S1. A corpus_judge row (gate=judge) is a KILL when the gate's output holds `JUDGE <member> <rule id> RED`
#      for the rule id in `expect_red`, on at least one bank member. `CONTROL` and `SELFCHECK` rows do not
#      count. The red ROWS are counted, one per finding.
#  S2. An applied_twin row (gate=twin) is a KILL when a TWIN PAIR's line is `✗ <member> #<ord> (<dir>):
#      identical served interactions, outcome, final state and trace — <n> finding(s) under <rules>` with the
#      rule id in `expect_red` among <rules>, on at least one pair, AND every member's self-pair line ("the
#      base program run twice is clean against itself") is ✓. A finding that also shows on a self-pair is
#      noise in the comparison, not a kill.
#  S3. Where `direction` is not `-`, that text must open the row's facts (`RED <direction>:`).
#  S4. A compile or type error, a timeout, a non-zero exit with no row for the named rule, or another rule
#      red alone is NOT a kill and is recorded as what it is. Exit status is not read as a verdict.
#  S5. `members` is the predicted set with the named rule red (for gate=twin, the members whose pair is
#      red). A different set with the rule red is a kill and a prediction miss. `rows:N` predicts the count
#      of red rows of the named rule.
#  S6. `also` is what else is predicted on the SAME gate. `none` predicts that no other rule id is red on
#      any member; anything else red is a prediction miss. `-` predicts nothing either way. A list ending
#      `; else -` predicts the listed items and nothing either way about the rest.
#  S7. `other_gate` is the prediction for the gate the row is not scored on. It decides nothing about the
#      kill; a miss there is a prediction miss.
#  S8. A control row passes on its `expect` text; a control that does not is a stop-and-report.
